sections.h2: Does Georgia have an estate tax or inheritance tax?
sections.html:
No. Georgia levies neither one today, and the Department of Revenue says so in plain terms on its estate tax FAQ.

The controlling statute is O.C.G.A. 48-12-1, which took effect July 1, 2014. It reads that on and after that date there shall be no estate taxes levied by the state and no estate tax returns required by the state. The Department adds that Georgia has no inheritance tax, which some people use as another word for estate tax.

For a family selling an inherited Georgia house, this means the state does not take a share of the estate before the property can be sold or distributed to heirs. The taxes that remain are the ones tied to the sale itself, to the property, and to federal law.

sections.h2: What was the old Georgia estate tax, and does it still matter?
sections.html:
It matters only for very old estates. The Department explains that the prior tax applied just to people who died before January 1, 2005, and it was tied to the federal credit for state death taxes on Form 706.

That federal credit was phased down for deaths in 2002, 2003 and 2004, then replaced with a deduction for deaths in 2005 and after. Georgia's tax followed the credit, so for any date of death after December 31, 2004, the Department says the state tax does not apply to an estate in a year when the Internal Revenue Code allows no credit for state death taxes.

For a death before 2005 the rules were different: the estate paid the tax before assets went to heirs, and the filing was a copy of the federal return sent with payment, due 9 months after the date of death. If a family is still closing an estate from that era, the Department's Estate Tax Section handles the file.

sections.h2: Does the federal estate tax reach a Georgia house?
sections.html:
Only a large estate owes federal estate tax. The IRS says most relatively simple estates do not need to file a return, and a filing is required when the gross estate, adding adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, exceeds the threshold for the year of death.

For 2026 the IRS table shows $15,000,000. The gross estate counts real estate, cash, securities, insurance, trusts and business interests at fair market value on the date of death, and deductions are allowed for mortgages and other debts, administration expenses, and property passing to a surviving spouse or qualified charities.

An estate with a surviving spouse can also elect to pass unused exemption to that spouse, and that election is made on a timely filed estate tax return even when no tax is due. An estate lawyer can tell you whether a Form 706 is worth filing for portability.

sections.h2: What taxes can an heir face when selling an inherited Georgia home?
sections.html:
The sale can create income tax on a gain, and the property keeps generating an annual tax bill. Georgia's estate tax is out of the picture, so these are the questions that remain.

  • Income inclusion: the Department says to check with the IRS on whether anything you inherited must be included in income.
  • Capital gain: the gain is the amount realized minus adjusted basis. For property acquired from a decedent, the IRS sends you to its publications on basis and on the holding period, since the one-year rule has exceptions.
  • Home exclusion: the $250,000 or $500,000 exclusion needs ownership and use for 24 months in the five years before sale, which an heir who never lived in the house may not meet.
  • Property tax: Georgia puts the full year's bill on whoever owned the property on January 1.

Georgia has no tax waiver requirement for transferring inherited assets such as stock, according to the Department. A brokerage that asks for a state waiver can be pointed to its FAQ.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for an inherited house?
sections.html:
The county bills the owner of record on January 1, and the Department says Georgia law gives no refund of property tax to a partial-year owner. If the owner died after January 1, the year's bill still has to be dealt with by the estate or the heir who sells.

Each county sets its own due date. The Department says taxes are normally due December 20 in most counties, with 60 days from the billing date to pay. Fulton County, as an example of a different schedule, set October 15, 2026 for most 2026 bills.

Before listing, ask the county tax commissioner what is owed on the parcel and whether any lien is filed with the clerk on the general execution docket. The Department also says county liens are handled by the issuing tax commissioner.

sections.h2: Are there Georgia withholding rules for heirs who live elsewhere?
sections.html:
Yes, when an heir who lives outside Georgia sells inherited Georgia real estate, the buyer generally withholds 3% of the purchase price under O.C.G.A. 48-7-128. The heir can instead provide a sworn affidavit of gain on Form IT-AFF2, and withholding is then 3% of the gain.

The Department lists several exceptions. Sales under $20,000 are exempt, as are sales where the tax would be under $600 and the seller signs the gain affidavit. Co-owners are tested separately, so a mix of resident and nonresident heirs affects only the nonresident share. The buyer files by the last day of the month after closing and gives the seller a statement to attach to the Georgia income tax return.

Ask the closing attorney to confirm each heir's residency status before the settlement statement is prepared.

faqs.q: Does Georgia charge an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. The Georgia Department of Revenue states that Georgia has no inheritance tax. Under O.C.G.A. 48-12-1, no state estate taxes are levied on or after July 1, 2014, and no state estate tax returns are required.

faqs.q: When did Georgia's estate tax end?
faqs.a: The statute eliminating it took effect July 1, 2014. The Department adds that the old tax only applied to deaths before January 1, 2005, because the federal state death tax credit it relied on was replaced with a deduction after that.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax waiver to transfer inherited stock in Georgia?
faqs.a: No. The Department of Revenue says Georgia has no inheritance or estate tax waiver requirements. If a brokerage asks for one, show it the Department's estate tax FAQ.

faqs.q: Is there a federal estate tax return requirement for a Georgia estate?
faqs.a: Only for large estates. The IRS shows a filing threshold of $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026, measured on the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption. A return can also be filed to elect portability for a surviving spouse.

faqs.q: Who owes property tax if the owner died during the year?
faqs.a: The bill follows the owner on January 1. The Department says Georgia law allows no refund to partial-year owners, so the estate or the heir selling should check the bill with the county tax commissioner and settle it at or before closing.
